correctness.rationale: On any path, covering all vertices is equivalent to hitting both endpoints; after the first hit the remaining optimal cost is the same end-to-end mean L_N. The one-sided and two-sided hitting candidates solve their exact minimizing Bellman equations; positive successive increments justify the optimal offered preference. A stopping verification gives optimality over arbitrary adapted policies, not only a fixed direction rule. The exact difference E_N(3)-E_N(1) gives the local failure and its parity formulas; for at most five vertices every reachable frontier conflict has a compatible unvisited-first optimal decision. The reproducible script replays 45,150 exact rational checks, including independent enumeration over stationary offered-neighbor policies for all up-to-nine-vertex paths. Finite tests supplement, not replace, the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: Sections 1–4 and 7 of arXiv:1911.05170 give the same stochastic model and general tree cover/hitting algorithmic conclusions, but not the exact path start-sensitive formula or the minimal six-vertex failure of unvisited-first control. The closest prior matching-model work yields only order bounds or algorithms and does not by itself imply the explicit finite classification. The alternative greedy-walk process uses different choices. Indexed and accessible earlier claims concerning cycles, complete bipartite graphs, and tripartite graphs have different graph families and cannot imply this path statement. Historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: The path is the canonical low-degree family for controlled random walks. Exact finite starting-position cover times, a simple complete optimal two-stage strategy, and a sharp first path-order obstruction to unvisited-first neighbor priority give new structural and algorithmic information beyond a coarse O(n) bound. The exact 4/3-step penalty at the first failure and asymptotic 4-step limit quantify a real local-control tradeoff, rather than an arbitrary small numerical refinement.
